title: Invariant coordinate forces a zero coefficient
statement: Let $r$ be a natural number, let $f:\{0,1\}^r\to\mathbb F_2$, let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$, and let $i\in S$. Suppose that for every input $x$, the value of $f$ is unchanged when coordinate $i$ is set to $1$ rather than to $0$, with all other coordinates fixed. Then the algebraic normal form coefficient of $f$ indexed by $S$ is $0$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $r$-dimensional cube
$S$ is a finite set of coordinates
$f$ is invariant under changing coordinate $i$ between $0$ and $1$ for every input
